brief: Trend core PCE inflation has been range-bound at 2.5-3% since 2021-2022, not converging toward the Fed's 2% target. That persistence pushed intermeeting Fed communication hawkish: July dissenters Logan and Hammack, Musalem's CNBC remarks, and Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole speech all pointed to insufficient progress. SG revised its call to a 25bp September hike with a hawkish SEP. Fed officials split into two camps: one expects inflation to slow in 2H26 and favors holding, the other sees a structural overshoot and favors tightening. Williams and Waller, in the hold camp, have set an implicit reaction function where a failure of core PCE to return toward target justifies a hike. Waller's dovish lean rests on the 3-month core PCE pace slowing from 4.6% in February to about 3% in July, but SG's trimmed-mean measures disagree on whether that slowdown is real, and policy-rule benchmarks show the fed funds rate not near neutral but below the level conditions justify. August PPI points to a firm super-core PCE print. SG expects the SEP's median dot to show two 2026 hikes, a 2027 hold, and a higher long-run rate, and its own path adds hikes at December and March, though March may not materialize.
